description: AMS1117 series, 1A Low Dropout Voltage Regulator; -3.3 = fixed 3.3V output variant (p1 FEATURES/ORDERING INFORMATION)

pinout.name: GND
pinout.notes: Datasheet's shared 3-pin list (p1, 'PIN CONNECTIONS / 3 PIN FIXED/ADJUSTABLE VERSION', governs both the SOT-223 Top View and TO-252 Front View drawings) labels this 'Ground/Adjust'. AMS1117-3.3 is the fixed-voltage part, so pin 1 = Ground. Application Hints (p3, Load Regulation): 'In the case of fixed voltage devices the top of R1 is connected Kelvin internally, and the ground pin can be used for negative side sensing.'

pinout.name: VOUT
pinout.notes: Regulated output, fixed 3.3V (p2 Electrical Characteristics: Min 3.201-3.251V / Typ 3.300V / Max 3.349-3.399V at IOUT=10mA, VIN=4.8V). The output capacitor on this pin is part of the frequency-compensation network, not just bypass (see decoupling).

pinout.name: VIN
pinout.notes: Unregulated input. Abs max 15V (p2). Dropout (VIN-VOUT) 1.1V typ / 1.3V max at IOUT=0.8A (p2-3).

pinout.name: TAB
pinout.notes: Metal tab: thermal path and an electrical terminal in its own right. IMPORTANT - drawing precision: the datasheet's explicit 'TAB IS OUTPUT' callout (p1, PIN CONNECTIONS) is drawn immediately beside the TO-252 FRONT VIEW only. The SOT-223 Top View on the same page is a top-down view showing only leads 1/2/3 along the bottom edge; it does not depict or separately label the tab (a top view of a bottom-tab package can't show it). So this PDF does not carry an SOT-223-specific 'tab is output' sentence. Tab=VOUT (same node as pin 2) is inferred from: (a) both package drawings sit under the one shared 3-pin function list (1-Ground/Adjust, 2-VOUT, 3-VIN) with no separate SOT-223 pin list, and (b) TO-252's tab is explicitly stated as OUTPUT for the same die/lead-frame family. Flagged in OPEN as an inference, not a literal SOT-223 label. Thermal Considerations (p5): the heat-spreading copper layer does NOT need to be electrically connected to the tab - PC material transmits heat effectively between the tab-attached pad and a separate plane despite the material's high bulk thermal resistivity, because the layer-to-layer length/area ratio is small.

decoupling.placement: output, per Figure 1 and Figure 2 application circuits (p3)
decoupling.notes: Stability section (p3): 'The circuit design used in the AMS1117 series requires the use of an output capacitor as part of the device frequency compensation. The addition of 22uF solid tantalum on the output will ensure stability for all operating conditions.' 22uF covers the case where the (adjustable-version) ADJ pin is bypassed for ripple rejection; without ADJ-pin bypass, smaller output caps 'can be used with equally good results' (no specific smaller value stated). Larger COUT further improves stability/transient response (no specific value stated). p2 Electrical Characteristics confirms COUT=22uF tantalum was the actual ripple-rejection test condition for the -3.3 fixed part (VIN=4.75V, IOUT=1A, 60dB min / 72dB typ).

land_pattern.notes: No RECOMMENDED LAND PATTERN (PCB copper footprint) drawing exists in this datasheet - pages 7-8 are titled 'PACKAGE DIMENSIONS' and give body/lead physical dimensions only, not copper pad recommendations. pitch_mm/pad_size_mm intentionally left unset rather than derived from the package outline (per grounding rule: land pattern must come from a recommended-land-pattern drawing, not the package outline). Raw package/lead dimensions transcribed for reference only (NOT copper pad sizes), from p7 '3 LEAD SOT-223 PLASTIC PACKAGE': overall body width 6.30-6.71mm (0.248-0.264in); narrower top-view width dim (tab width) 2.95-3.15mm (0.116-0.124in); overall body length 6.71-7.29mm (0.264-0.287in); inner length dim 3.30-3.71mm (0.130-0.146in); lead width 0.84-1.04mm (0.033-0.041in) shown twice flanking a center dim of 2.29mm NOM (0.090in NOM, appears to be lead pitch); body height 1.80mm MAX (0.071in MAX); underside length dim 4.60mm NOM (0.181in NOM); foot length 0.31mm MIN (0.012in MIN); foot dims 0.64-0.84mm (0.025-0.033in) x2; lead foot angles 10-16deg and 10deg MAX; foot width 0.25-0.36mm (0.010-0.014in). pad_count=4 = 3 leads (pins 1-3, p1 PIN CONNECTIONS) + 1 tab pad.

exposed_pad.connect_to: VOUT (tab electrically = pin 2 / VOUT; see pinout[TAB].notes and OPEN for how this is inferred vs. literally labeled in this PDF). Thermal Considerations (p5): the PCB heat-spreading copper does NOT need to be electrically connected to the tab.

layout_notes: Abs-max SOT-223 thermal resistance is stated as phi-JA=90C/W with a footnote (p2): 'With package soldering to copper area over backside ground plane or internal power plane phi-JA can vary from 46C/W to >90C/W depending on mounting technique and the size of the copper area.'

Thermal Considerations (p5): thermal resistance junction-to-tab for AMS1117 is 15C/W; tab-to-ambient can be as low as 30C/W; total junction-to-ambient can be as low as 45C/W with a reasonably sized PC board having at least one copper layer to spread heat into the surrounding air.
For the SOT-223 surface-mount package, additional heat sources mounted near the device must be considered (thermal interactions with other board components affect the achievable Rth).

Heat-spreading copper layer does NOT need to be electrically connected to the tab: PC material is effective at transmitting heat between the tab-attached pad and a ground/power plane (inside the board or on the opposite side) despite high bulk PC-material thermal resistivity, because the layer-to-layer length/area ratio is small.

Table 1 thermal-resistance-vs-copper-area guideline (p5; measured on 1/16in FR-4, 1oz copper foil; tab of device attached to topside copper): 2500sqmm top + 2500sqmm backside + 2500sqmm board area = 55C/W; 1000sqmm top + 2500sqmm backside + 2500sqmm board area = 55C/W; 225sqmm top + 2500sqmm backside + 2500sqmm board area = 65C/W; 100sqmm top + 2500sqmm backside + 2500sqmm board area = 80C/W; 1000sqmm top + 1000sqmm backside + 1000sqmm board area = 60C/W; 1000sqmm top + 0 backside + 1000sqmm board area = 65C/W.
Power/thermal formulas (p5): PD = (VIN - VOUT) x IOUT; TJ = TA(MAX) + PD x Rth(junction-to-ambient); TJ must not exceed 125C under continuous normal load.
Thermal shutdown trips when junction temperature exceeds 165C at the sense point (p3, Application Hints).

Load regulation is measured at the output lead approximately 1/8 inch from the package (p2 Note 3); for fixed-voltage devices the top of R1 is Kelvin-connected internally and the ground pin can be used for negative-side (return) sensing (p3).
